title: Did you know… Stephen saw heaven open before his death?
paragraphs: Did you know… Stephen saw heaven open before his death?
He wasn’t screaming.
He was seeing.
Right there, as stones tore through his body, Stephen looked up… and heaven opened.

Not metaphor.
Not poetry.
Reality.
In Book of Acts 7:55–56, Scripture says he was “full of the Holy Spirit” and saw the glory of God—and Jesus Christ standing at the right hand of God.
Standing.
Not seated like in every other passage.
Standing… as if heaven itself rose to welcome a dying servant home.
But don’t miss this.

Stephen wasn’t just a victim.
He was a witness.
Before the vision, he preached truth that cut deep. He exposed sin. He called out hardened hearts. And it cost him everything.

Stones fell.
Blood spilled.
Breath faded.
Yet his final words?
“Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”

That’s not human strength.
That’s the Gospel alive inside a man.

Because the same Jesus he saw…
was the same Jesus who, on the cross, said, “Father, forgive them.”
This is the scandal of grace:

A man unjustly killed… forgiving his killers.
A broken body… filled with heaven’s vision.
A violent end… becoming a doorway to glory.
And here’s where it hits us.

We want comfort without surrender.
Vision without sacrifice.
Heaven… without the cross.
But Stephen shows us—when your eyes are fixed on Christ, even death loses its terror.
Because you don’t fall into darkness.
You step into glory.

So the question is not: Will heaven open?
The question is: Will you be looking up when it does?
Turn your eyes to Jesus now—while there’s still breath in your lungs. Repent. Believe. Receive the grace that transforms fear into faith.

Because the same Christ who stood for Stephen…
still stands ready to receive you.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
